description: Systematic startup validation methodology combining principles from Thiel, Abraham, Naval, Graham, Bier, and Willison

contributors.name: Peter Thiel
contributors.principle: Start with a small market you can dominate
contributors.quote: Competition is for losers. If you want to create and capture lasting value, look to build a monopoly.

contributors.name: Jay Abraham
contributors.principle: Position as trusted authority, not vendor
contributors.quote: If you truly believe that what you have is useful and valuable to your clients, then you have a moral obligation to try to serve them in every way possible.

contributors.name: Naval Ravikant
contributors.principle: Seek business models with zero marginal cost
contributors.quote: Code and media are permissionless leverage. They're the leverage behind the newly rich.

contributors.name: Paul Graham
contributors.quote: The way to get startup ideas is not to try to think of startup ideas. It's to look for problems, preferably problems you have yourself.

contributors.name: Nikit Bier
contributors.principle: Identify and invert limiting industry assumptions
contributors.quote: The most valuable businesses redefine the rules of their category rather than competing within existing constraints.

contributors.name: Simon Willison
contributors.principle: Accelerate development cycles through appropriate tools
contributors.quote: The biggest advantage is speed of development. It's not about getting work done faster, it's about being able to ship projects that I wouldn't have been able to justify spending time on at all.

components.name: Category Creation Validation
components.description: Validating the creation of a new market category with a monopolistic position

components.name: Product Strategy Validation
components.description: Validating that the product solves a real problem and creates significant value

components.name: Leverage Systems Validation
components.description: Validating the leverage mechanisms that enable exponential rather than linear growth

components.name: Marketing Strategy Validation
components.description: Validating positioning, messaging, and conversion approaches

MVP.description: Minimum Viable Product is a function of core value delivered, user pain resolved, and minimal feature set

variables.CoreValue: The primary value proposition of the solution
variables.UserPain: The intensity and frequency of the customer problem
variables.MinimalFeatures: The smallest set of features required to deliver the core value

MVP.calculation: Qualitative assessment scored 1-10 for each variable, multiplied together, divided by 10
MVP.threshold: MVP Score > 60 indicates viable product concept

PMF.description: Product-Market Fit is the sum of user engagement metrics, retention rates, referral rates, and disappointment if removed

variables.UserEngagement: Frequency and depth of product usage (0-10)
variables.Retention: Percentage of users who remain active after 30 days (0-1)
variables.Referral: Net Promoter Score or referral rate (0-10)
variables.Disappointment: User reported disappointment if product disappeared (0-10)

PMF.threshold: PMF Score > 7 indicates strong product-market fit

CAC_LTV.description: Customer Acquisition Cost should be less than one-third of Customer Lifetime Value for a viable acquisition model

variables.CAC: Total marketing and sales costs / Number of new customers
variables.LTV: Average revenue per customer * Gross margin * Average customer lifespan

Growth.description: Growth compounds based on initial traction, virality coefficient, and retention rate over time

variables.Virality: K-factor, number of new users each existing user brings (> 1 for viral growth)
variables.Retention: Percentage of users retained each period (0-1)

Growth.threshold: Virality > 1.1 and Retention > 0.85 indicates sustainable growth

Monopoly.description: Monopoly position strength is a function of category creation, 10x value delivery, and network effects

variables.CategoryCreation: Degree to which you've created a new category (0-10)
variables.10xValue: Factor by which your solution is better than alternatives on key dimension (1-10)
variables.NetworkEffects: Strength of network effects in your business model (0-10)

Monopoly.threshold: Monopoly Score > 7 indicates strong defensible position

MarketingROI.description: Return on investment for marketing activities

variables.Revenue: Revenue directly attributable to marketing activities
variables.MarketingCost: Total cost of marketing campaigns and activities

ExponentialValue.description: Value creation that compounds exponentially over time

ValidationScore.description: Overall validation score across four key dimensions

variables.ProblemValidation: Evidence that the problem exists and is painful (0-10)
variables.SolutionValidation: Evidence that the solution resolves the problem effectively (0-10)
variables.MarketValidation: Evidence that enough people have this problem to support a business (0-10)
variables.BusinessModelValidation: Evidence that customers will pay enough to create a viable business (0-10)

DefensibilityIndex.description: Measure of business defensibility across multiple dimensions

CategoryClarity.description: Clarity and effectiveness of category creation

mvt_tasks.task: Define category name and core positioning statement (10 words or less)
Create contrarian truth one-pager with supporting evidence
mvt_tasks.validation_method: Industry expert feedback and customer reaction

mvt_tasks.task: Develop 3 clear problem statements from customer interviews
mvt_tasks.validation_method: Minimum 10 customer interviews with consistent patterns
Engagement metrics on initial content pieces

mvt_tasks.task: Design conversion funnel with clear stage definitions
mvt_tasks.validation_method: Conversion rate estimates and early testing

mvt_tasks.task: Create risk-reversal mechanism for early adopters
Define viral loop mechanic in product/marketing
Establish key metrics dashboard for marketing validation
Develop systematic A/B testing protocol for messaging

components.name: Problem Validation
questions: Is the problem real and painful?
Is the problem frequent enough?
Are customers actively seeking solutions?
Is the problem growing in importance?
Is the problem clearly articulated?

components.name: Solution Validation
questions: Does the solution effectively solve the problem?
Is the solution 10x better on at least one dimension?
Is the solution easy to adopt?
Does the solution create demonstrable results?
Is the solution scalable?

components.name: Market Validation
questions: Is the market large enough?
Is the initial market segment clearly defined?
Is the market growing?
Can we reach customers efficiently?
Are there few or weak competitors?

components.name: Business Model Validation
questions: Will customers pay enough?
Are acquisition costs sustainable?
Does the model have strong unit economics?
Is there potential for high margins?
Is there a clear path to scaling revenue?

prompt: Create a validation plan for [MY STARTUP] using the TANGO-PLUS framework. Analyze the potential for category creation, identify the contrarian truth, and design a minimum viable product that addresses a painful problem. Include specific validation metrics and experiments for testing core assumptions across all four validation quadrants: category creation, product strategy, leverage systems, and marketing strategy. Develop a 6-week roadmap prioritizing MVT tasks, with emphasis on rapid prototyping and evidence-based iteration. Calculate preliminary scores using the framework formulas and conclude with an action plan prioritizing critical validation tasks.
